subject: Privatenet telemetry anomaly impacting control-plane reconnections
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
To: Rajiv Shah <rajiv@gridpointhealth.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 5 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: [URGENT] Observed spike in privatenet telemetry → control-plane reconnection failures

Hi Rajiv / GridPoint ops team,

I wanted to let you know we observed an uptick in control-plane reconnection failures for your Private deployment starting ~08:50 PDT this morning after the private agent upgrade that rolled to 3 of your nodes. Symptoms we saw in our telemetry: repeated handshake timeouts between the on-prem agent and the management plane, a short-lived surge in control RPC errors, and increased reconnect attempts (see attached snapshot).

What we've done so far:
- Flagged the canary cohort and paused further rollout across your cluster.
- Scoped the impact: ~18% of requests routed through the upgraded agents saw an extra 200–600ms latency and ~2–3% experienced transient connection failures (no data loss observed).
- Deployed a temporary routing rule to failover affected agent traffic to the standby pool to reduce customer impact.

Immediate next steps we are executing (ETA +30–60 min):
1) Full rollback of the canary agents to the prior build (no config change) — Marcus leading.
2) Post-rollback verification runbooks executed against control-plane health endpoints and agent heartbeats.
3) Collection of detailed traces and KV-cache divergence evidence (we've attached a CSV snapshot).

We will not perform any disruptive on-prem restarts without explicit consent — rollback operates at agent process level and is designed to be seamless for data plane connections. If you prefer we can schedule a maintenance window for a graceful restart; otherwise we'll proceed with the rollback and staged verification.

Apologies for the interruption — our priority is minimizing any customer-visible impact. I will keep you updated through this thread and share the RCA once the investigation completes.

Attachments: privatenet-telemetry-snapshot-0505.csv (CSV outline of sampling windows and error counts)
Runbook: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/0B-example-runbook
Jira: PRIVNET-4523

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
jordan@redwood.com

From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Rajiv Shah <rajiv@gridpointhealth.com>
Date: Fri, 5 May 2028 09:38:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: [URGENT] Observed spike in privatenet telemetry → control-plane reconnection failures

On Fri, May 5, 2028 at 09:12 AM Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com> wrote:
> I wanted to let you know we observed an uptick in control-plane reconnection failures for your Private deployment starting ~08:50 PDT this morning after the private agent upgrade that rolled to 3 of your nodes.

Thanks Jordan — quick operational note from my side: we confirmed the agent binary introduced an aggressive backoff path that under certain heartbeat jitter causes the control-plane handshake to exceed the retry window. That path is fixed in the candidate patch; however, since this is a production-private deployment we will roll the canary back to the previous build (v2.11.3) as a precaution.

Planned rollback sequence (non-disruptive):
- 09:45 UTC: trigger rollback on canary nodes (agent process graceful restart, config unchanged).
- 09:48–10:15 UTC: automated health checks — heartbeat rate, handshake success ratio, control RPC latencies.
- 10:20 UTC: if green, extend rollback to remaining nodes in small batches under observation.

I will own the rollback and will post logs + a summary here. If GridPoint needs a simultaneous maintenance window, please tell us now; otherwise we proceed as above.

-Marcus
Sr. Software Engineer, Runtime
marcus@redwood.com

From: Rajiv Shah <rajiv@gridpointhealth.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 5 May 2028 09:51:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: [URGENT] Observed spike in privatenet telemetry → control-plane reconnection failures

Thanks for the quick heads-up. A couple questions:
1) Will the rollback cause any restarts of our customer-facing services? We need to coordinate if there will be brief interruptions.
2) Rough ETA on a postmortem? Our compliance team will want the trace evidence for the last 24 hours.

If rollback is non-disruptive as you said, please proceed. We appreciate the routing rule to the standby pool — that minimized impact on our traffic.

— Rajiv
Director, Site Reliability — GridPoint Health
rajiv@gridpointhealth.com
ops@gridpointhealth.com

From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
To: Rajiv Shah <rajiv@gridpointhealth.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 6 May 2028 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: [URGENT] Observed spike in privatenet telemetry → control-plane reconnection failures — rollback complete + preliminary RCA

Rajiv — thanks for the patience. Quick update and preliminary findings: rollback completed at 09:55 UTC on 2028-05-05 and automated checks returned to normal within ~8 minutes. Observations and root cause summary below (preliminary):

What happened:
- A change in the agent’s heartbeat backoff calculation (introduced in v2.12.0-canary) made certain jittered network conditions hit the handshake retry ceiling earlier than intended, producing repeated reconnect attempts and transient control RPC errors.

Impact:
- Incident window: 2028-05-05 08:50–09:55 PDT
- Customer-visible symptom: small fraction (~2–3%) of requests experienced transient 5xx-like behavior for <1 minute before the failover rule kicked in. No persistent data loss.

Remediation completed:
- Canary rollback to v2.11.3 — completed and verified.
- Deployed conservative heartbeat backoff guard in the canary pipeline; blocking full rollout until additional staging validation is complete.

Artifacts attached: privnet-rca-0506.pdf (preliminary RCA with traces) and the telemetry CSV we sent earlier. Evidence bucket and logs: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/0B-example-runbook (read-only link). Jira ticket: PRIVNET-4523 — we will append full postmortem notes when the investigation is closed.

Next steps for GridPoint and Redwood:
- We will schedule a 30-minute bridge Tuesday 2028-05-09 16:00 PDT to walk through the RCA and answer any compliance questions (calendar invite to follow).
- Redwood will produce a final postmortem with corrected timelines, impact quantification, and test additions to prevent regression.

If you need the raw traces or more granular logs sooner, Marcus and I can provide scoped bundles.

Apologies again for the disruption — we treat this seriously and will follow up with a final RCA.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
jordan@redwood.com
